THERMAL CHARACTERIZATION / M1 EQUIVALENCE
◈

M1 equivalent layer

90-SPHERE CALIBRATION · ORTHOTROPIC K

Left: historical four-tile calibration specimen with 90 enclosed spheres at their original supplied coordinates (transparent matrix). Right: homogeneous equivalent four-tile specimen. Production M1 uses the equivalent material; spheres are not measured CT data.

Local void fraction30%
Verification2 meshes
01 Directional conductivity

Medium/fine values from six directional 1 K steady-state tests; this checks local conductivity stability only.

02 Historical matched MX / ME test

Paired explicit-sphere MX and equivalent ME belong to a separate historical configuration, not the present M2/M3 through-hole cases.

ⓘ
Two-mesh conductivity stability does not prove full-package mesh independence or M1 transfer accuracy at every position. The matched replacement maximum nodal error was 0.031350 K (41.33% of the maximum explicit defect signal).
NUMERICAL CHECKS / MESH SENSITIVITY
▥

Mesh sensitivity

M0 · 10% F-M2 · 10% F-M3

Nine actual full-PM3 solves refine Si, TIM1, and void boundaries. Coarse, medium, and fine meshes are compared at fixed physics.

Returned runs9/9
Declared screensPASS
01 Peak silicon temperature

Real three-level sequences, including the non-monotonic M0 result. No artificial convergence fit.

02 Fixed-ROI FE mean

The same physical Si ROI (80.08 mm³) is integrated on all nine meshes.

03 Fine–medium screening

Declared limits: |Δ peak| ≤ 0.05 K and |Δ ROI mean| ≤ 0.02 K, for these models only.

04 M3 − M2 morphology contrast

The fine-minus-medium peak contrast changes by −0.022938 K (0.2773% of fine contrast); this is not an M1-equivalence test.

ⓘ
Targeted mesh-sensitivity screens passed for M0, F-M2 and F-M3. Uniform global mesh independence, all-position convergence, local heat-flux convergence and experimental validation have not been established.
